title: The Juiciest Corporate Scandals with Becca Platsky
summary: Eisman and Platsky use fraud cases, media mergers, prediction markets and FIFA to discuss oversight and executive accountability. Platsky corrects her Frank customer counts during the interview. Eisman favors the Paramount combination and challenges weak corporate governance, but makes overbroad claims about the absence of financial-crisis prosecutions. Official records verify the Javice case and contemporaneous merger delay, correct Immelt tenure, and contradict claims of universal executive impunity. Many psychological explanations, private anecdotes and current corruption allegations remain unverified.
assessment: Valuable governance questions with uneven factual precision. Preserve explicit corrections and distinguish subjective criticism from legal findings. Guest allegations are not Eisman views by silence. His broad enforcement language conflicts with documented prosecutions, while the narrower accountability of leading Wall Street executives remains unresolved.
speaker_map_notes: SPEAKER_00 repeatedly self-identifies as Eisman and introduces Becca Platsky, who answers as SPEAKER_01. Dialogue clarifies occasional embedded short interjections.
framework_points: Compare public executive statements with filings and actual conduct.
Separate fraud identification from short-sale timing.
Distinguish buyer due diligence failures from perpetrator culpability.
Test board independence and relevant expertise.
Use pressure, opportunity and rationalization as risk questions, not proof of guilt.
Distinguish allegations, charges, convictions and policy preferences.
tools_and_charts: Acquisition customer data and due-diligence verification
transcript_cautions: Platsky explicitly corrects initial Frank figures at 888-903 seconds; retain the revision.
The acquisition is briefly misstated as $177 million; the surrounding account and official record use $175 million.
FAFSA is an application for financial aid, not a standalone loan type.
Captions contain missing passages around 769-792, 1377-1386 and 1527-1542 seconds.
Carr is called an FTC commissioner, but is FCC chairman.
Blazer role and Immelt tenure are misstated.
Discussion of future trial and merger fees predates the September settlement; do not retroactively treat the original procedural claim as false.
